The fail-open trade-off is documented (revocation.js header) and the compensating controls are real and now runtime-tested, BUT two concrete holes existed: (1) the boot fail-fast predicate in index.js did not cover the REDIS_URL-only shape, so a configured-but-dead Redis booted, reported health=503, and still served with per-request fail-open revocation; (2) no commandTimeout, so a blackholed Redis hung auth indefinitely.
